newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Dollar to stay firm vs mark all year - German banker.
newsitem.headline: Dollar to stay firm vs mark all year - German banker.

text.p: The dollar is likely to remain firm against the mark all year because of the divergent interest rate trends in the U.S. and Germany, a senior German banker said on Monday.

"The interest rate trend in the U.S. is upwards, the D-mark interest rate trend I would say for the next one-and-a-half years will be flat and this reflects the different state of the economies," Ernst-Moritz Lipp, management board member of Dresdner Bank AG, told Reuters Financial Television (RFTV).
"With the widening of the interest (rate) differential between the two currencies I expect the U.S. dollar to be firm over, let's say, all this year."
He added there could be "some further rise" in the dollar against the mark.
Lipp also said the dollar's strength against the mark had nothing to do with market uncertainty over European monetary union.
Lipp was speaking to RFTV at the World Economic Forum in Davos.
